Our TISUK accreditation recognises our whole-school commitment to creating a safe, supportive learning environment where relationships come first. Trauma-informed practice underpins everything we do, helping every young person feel understood, ready to learn and able to thrive.
Springboard Education is a specialist school providing personalised education for young people with social, emotional, mental health and communication needs. Through strong relationships, high expectations and individual support, we help every student learn, grow and thrive.

Welcome to our photo gallery, where we celebrate the wonderful moments and achievements of our students at Springboard. Here, you'll find a collection of photos that capture the spirit, creativity, and joy of our students. Each image tells a story of their daily experiences, milestones, and the strong sense of community that brings us all together. We hope you enjoy these glimpses into our vibrant and inclusive world, and come away inspired by the incredible journeys of our students. Enjoy exploring our gallery!

At Springboard Education CSR is a term used to describe when businesses look beyond their initial duty to Staff, Students and the Community. We are committed to ensure that our school aims to carry out activities as ethical, sustainable and for the benefit of all stakeholders.
We feel that we have a duty to take social responsibly seriously and see it as an integral part of our business.
Our students are encouraged to consider their own social impact through tutor-time, PSHE lessons and by following the Springboard Way. Recycling is embedded throughout the school and we endeavour to reduce our carbon footprint. The Curriculum and Continuous Professional Development is used to promote knowledge, attitudes and skills to enable individuals to make informed decisions relating to the impact their actions have on the environment and our community.
Fundraising is organised at the school for various charities throughout the year and decided on by the School Council, and individual classes. Both local and national charities have benefitted from our contributions.
​How can businesses help raise money for Springboard Education?
As a small independent school, we are happy to work in partnership will other businesses who wish to make a positive impact on the lives of our young people, we are currently fundraising for a Sensory Garden and Sensory Room. If you feel that your business or organisation can help raise funds or make a donation for our students, please use the contact us form to express your interest.
If you feel that your business may be able to provide time or assistance to help with our projects do get in contact using the form.

Our curriculum equips young people with the skills to manage their own futures. Springboard encourages an ethic of nurturing, safety, laughter and flexibility.
Each young person works at their own individual level within mixed age ability groupings. They have the opportunity to sit examinations and gain qualifications.
Oaks equips each young person with a portfolio of accredited work and certificated awards that will enable them to enter their chosen field of work, or study at their appropriate level by the time they leave.

Springboard Education are thrilled to announce our partnership with the Anna Freud Centre to enhance mental health support for our students and their families.
Together with the Anna Freud Centre we are able to provide students with access to remote counselling services. This is particularly beneficial for those who may feel more comfortable seeking help from the privacy of their own space.
Students can access remote counselling through Springboard by speaking with a trusted staff member, who can facilitate the referral process. Once referred, students have the opportunity to connect with trained mental health professionals via secure online platforms. This flexible approach allows students to receive timely and tailored support, making it easier for them to engage with mental health services without the barriers of traditional in-person appointments. By combining in-school support with remote counselling options, the Early Support Service aims to meet young people where they are, ensuring they have the resources they need to thrive.
The following videos explain a bit more about the service...
Students, parents and carers can also access support whenever they need it with our library of on-demand webinars. Topics cover the breadth of challenges young people face, including managing anger, dealing with negative thoughts and overcoming exam stress.
Please speak to a member of the Springboard team if you would like our support to access these services.

Springboard is a school for children aged between 9 and 18 who have a range of special educational needs. All students should have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Students may have learning difficulties and/or low attainment as a result of either their Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs.
Students who attend Springboard are usually referred to us by their local authority. We currently receive referrals from West Sussex, Brighton & Hove, Hampshire and East Sussex. We will also consider admissions from Parents/Carers direct and other local providers.
If we consider that the prospective student meets our admissions criteria, we will arrange for the child to visit us with their parents or carers. They will be able to tour the school, meet our key staff and talk about our school policies and curriculum.
If all parties agree that our school can meet the child’s needs, and that the child and parents/carers are committed to the placement, the necessary admission arrangements will be made.
To enquire about a child attending our school please contact us on 01903 605980 or email office@springboardeducation.co.uk

At Springboard, we believe that emotional wellbeing is the foundation for learning. That’s why our therapeutic provision is as individual as our students. Grounded in trauma-informed practice and driven by relational connection, our support extends far beyond the classroom.
We offer a range of tailored interventions designed to build trust, foster emotional regulation, and nurture creativity and confidence — always at the student’s pace and in tune with their needs.
One-to-one relational support from trusted adults, helping students to feel seen, heard and safe.
Art & Creative Therapies
Student-led, sensory and expressive sessions that help students process emotions and build confidence
Dog-assisted Therapy
We partner with Fetch Therapy to offer sessions with a trained therapy dog — supporting regulation, connection and wellbeing
A safe and child-led space where students can express and process big feelings through play. Guided by a trained practitioner, these sessions support emotional healing, regulation and trust-building
